questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion of $(2 - 3x)(1 + x)^{6}$.

options.why: Considered only the product of $2$ with $15x^{2}$, omitting the contribution from $-3x \times 6x$.
Added $30 + 18$ instead of subtracting $18$ from $30$.
Considered only the cross product $-3x \times 6x$, omitting $2 \times 15x^{2}$.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $(1 + 4x)(1 - 2x)^{5}$.

options.why: Omitted the contribution from $4x \times 40x^{2}$, keeping only the direct $x^{3}$ term.
Subtracted $160$ instead of adding: $-80 - 160 = -240$.
Considered only the cross term $4x \times 40x^{2}$, omitting $1 \times (-80x^{3})$.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion of $(2 + x - x^{2})(1 + 3x)^{4}$.

options.why: Added the constant $1$ instead of subtracting $1 \times 1$ for the $-x^{2}$ factor.
Considered only the constant factor $2 \times 54x^{2}$, omitting contributions from $x$ and $-x^{2}$.
Omitted the $-x^{2} \times 1$ contribution entirely from the combined sum.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion of $(1 - x)^{3}(1 + 3x)^{4}$.

options.why: Added $36$ instead of subtracting: $54 + 36 + 3 = 93$ or $54+3=57$.
Omitted the $3x^{2} \times 1$ contribution, calculating only $54 - 36 = 18$.
Reversed the signs of the terms when combining contributions.

questions.question_text: Find the constant term in the expansion of $(1 + x)^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x}\right)^{2}$.

options.why: Considered only the product of the two constant terms $1 \times 1$.
Omitted the $x^{2} \times \frac{9}{x^{2}}$ contribution, calculating $1 + 12 = 13$.
Used $2 \times 3 = 6$ instead of $2 \times 6 = 12$ for the middle cross term.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $(1 + 2x)^{2}(1 - x)^{5}$.

options.why: Considered only $1 \times (-10x^{3})$, ignoring the other two cross-term contributions.
Added all terms as positive: $10 + 40 - 20 = 30$ or dropped negative signs.
Subtracted $40$ instead of adding: $-10 - 40 - 20 = -70$.

questions.question_text: Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x}\right)^{3}$.

options.why: Added the cross terms instead of subtracting: $1 + 6 - 3 = 4$.
Omitted all cross-term contributions, calculating only the constant product $1 \times 1 = 1$.
Multiplied $-\frac{2}{3} \times 9 = -6$ and omitted the $+3$ contribution from $x^{2} \times \frac{27}{x^{2}}$.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $(1 + 2x)^{4}(1 - 3x)^{3}$.

options.why: Considered only the constant term times $-27x^{3}$, ignoring the other three cross terms.
Considered only $32x^{3} \times 1$, ignoring the other three cross terms.
Made a sign error when summing $+216 - 216 - 27 + 32$.

questions.question_text:
In the expansion of $(3 + ax)(1 + x)^{5}$, the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $10$.
What is the value of $a$?

options.why: Solved $5a = 20$ instead of $5a = -20$ when isolating $a$.
Used $\binom{5}{1}=5$ for the coefficient of $x^{2}$ instead of $\binom{5}{2}=10$.
Subtracted $30$ incorrectly as $10 - 30 = -30$ before dividing by $5$.

questions.question_text: Given $\dfrac1{1-x}\approx1+x+x^2$ and $\sqrt{1-3x}\approx1-\dfrac32x-\dfrac98x^2$, what is the coefficient of $x^2$ in the expansion of $\dfrac{\sqrt{1-3x}}{1-x}$?

options.why: Uses only the linear coefficient from the square-root expansion.
Uses only the quadratic coefficient from one factor and omits cross and denominator terms.
Uses the quadratic term from the reciprocal expansion alone.
